question: What is the total length of Golden Quadrilateral, built by the National Highways Authority of India(NHAI)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**5846 km**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The total length of the **Golden Quadrilateral**, built by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI), is **5846 km**.
 
• The Golden Quadrilateral is a highway network connecting major industrial, agricultural, and cultural centers of India.
 
• It forms a quadrilateral connecting Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, and Kolkata, facilitating efficient transport and trade across these major cities.
 
• The project was initiated by the Government of India under the National Highways Development Project (NHDP).
 
• It significantly reduces travel time and distance between the major cities, boosting economic activities and development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Golden Quadrilateral was the first phase of the National Highways Development Project (NHDP), which was launched in 1999.
 
• The project aimed to improve the quality and capacity of the national highways in India.
 
• It has contributed significantly to the economic growth of the country by improving connectivity and reducing transportation costs.
 
• The project was completed in January 2012, and it has since been a vital part of India's infrastructure.
 
• Further enhancements and expansions to the highway network continue to support India's growing economy and transportation needs.
